title: No sound from speakers or headphones in Windows
patterns: no audio output device is installed
summary: Windows plays audio but you hear nothing. Usually the wrong output device is selected, or the audio service or driver needs a reset.
cause: Windows can send sound to the wrong device (for example a monitor or an unplugged headset). A stalled audio service or damaged driver can also stop all sound.
steps: Click the speaker icon in the taskbar and make sure volume isn't muted. Then click the arrow next to the volume slider and pick the correct speakers or headphones.
Run the built-in fixer: Settings > System > Sound > Troubleshoot common sound problems.
Turn off audio enhancements: Settings > System > Sound, click your device, and set Enhance audio to Off. Test again.
Check that the device is enabled: Sound settings > More sound settings > Playback, right-click your device and choose Enable if it shows as disabled.

Reinstall the driver: Device Manager > Sound, video and game controllers > right-click your audio device > Uninstall device, then restart. If that fails, install the audio driver from your motherboard or laptop maker.
ifStillBroken: Try a different port or device, such as a USB headset, to see if the problem is the speakers or Windows.
